sourcedFrom: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover (2024 — read off the back-cover date code '01.24'; no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: Henry's H023 book. A lever action that feeds from a detachable box magazine and splits into two halves at the receiver: two receiver pins come out with a punch, and the bolt carrier rides out on the rear half with the trigger guard and stock. The bolt then comes apart from its carrier for cleaning. Henry recommends nothing past that. Page numbers here are the book's printed folios.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, safety pulled back to S
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, and pull the tang safety switch to the rear until the imprinted S shows. It clicks into place. Henry notes it only goes to SAFE with the hammer cocked or the lever open, so if it will not move, do not force it — and a safety that will not engage is no proof the rifle is empty.
steps.aside: The safety can only be switched to the “SAFE” position with the internal hammer cocked (after stroking the lever) or with the lever open.
steps.quote: pull the safety switch to the rear. Doing so will expose an imprinted 'S'.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS, SAFETY, p.12

steps.title: Magazine released ahead of the lever and pulled free
steps.action: The magazine release sits ahead of the lever, under the receiver. Push it forward and pull the magazine down out of the well. Do this before you work the lever — opening and closing the lever with a loaded magazine in only feeds another round into the chamber you are trying to empty.
steps.quote: push forward on the magazine release located ahead of the lever. Pull the magazine free.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO UNLOAD YOUR HENRY LEVER ACTION SUPREME RIFLE, p.15

steps.title: Lever opened, chamber emptied and inspected
steps.action: Rotate the lever fully forward to the open position. That extracts and ejects any cartridge or fired case left in the chamber. Then look into the chamber and the empty magazine well and confirm both are clear before you go any further. Leave the lever open.
steps.quote: Rotate the lever forward to the "open" position to extract and eject a cartridge or fired case that may be remaining in the chamber.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO UNLOAD YOUR HENRY LEVER ACTION SUPREME RIFLE, p.15
steps.warn: ALWAYS ASSUME THE CHAMBER IS LOADED, EVEN AFTER REMOVING THE MAGAZINE FROM THE RECEIVER

steps.title: Ammunition out of the workspace, eyes protected
steps.action: Before any tool touches the rifle, take every live round off the bench and out of the room you are working in. Henry asks for safety glasses for the whole job because parts in this rifle are under spring tension. Check once more that the rifle is unloaded — muzzle safe, finger off the trigger.
steps.quote: REMOVE ALL LIVE AMMUNITION FROM THE WORKSPACE.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, DISASSEMBLY, p.19
steps.warn: KEEP ALL AMMUNITION AWAY FROM THE CLEANING AREA. NEVER TEST THE MECHANICAL FUNCTION OF YOUR RIFLE WITH LIVE AMMUNITION.

steps.title: Lever open, magazine set aside
steps.action: Henry's disassembly starts with the lever open and the magazine out and put to one side. If the magazine went back in after unloading, take it out again now. The lever stays open for the next step.
steps.quote: Open the lever and remove the magazine to be set aside.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, DISASSEMBLY, p.19

steps.title: Both receiver pins driven out with a punch
steps.action: Drive the two receiver pins out of the receiver with a punch. Henry calls them non-directional, so they can be driven from either side. Support the rifle on a padded surface while you tap, and keep the pins together — they go back in at the end and tap home flush.
steps.quote: Drive the two non-directional receiver pins out with
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, DISASSEMBLY, p.19

steps.title: Forearm and stock wrist pulled apart
steps.action: Hold the forearm in one hand and the wrist of the stock in the other, and work them apart with a push-pull motion. The rifle separates into two halves: the barrel, forearm and receiver in one, and the trigger guard, bolt carrier and stock in the other. Do not twist or pry — if it will not move, check that both pins are fully out.
steps.quote: use one hand to hold the forearm and the other hand to hold the stock wrist. Use a push/pull motion to separate the two halves.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Bore cleaned breech to muzzle, never a brush first
steps.action: Clean the bore in the direction the bullet travels, from the chamber end out to the muzzle. Henry recommends a pull-through kit; a rod and patches will do, but keep the rod off the muzzle crown and keep fouling from being pushed back into the action. Never start with a brush — the brush carries dirt and residue into the chamber and receiver.
steps.quote: WHENEVER POSSIBLE, CLEAN THE BORE IN THE DIRECTION OF BULLET TRAVEL.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — BORE CLEANING, p.21
steps.warn: NEVER RUN A BRUSH IN THE BARREL FIRST.

steps.title: Bolt wiped clean and lightly oiled
steps.action: With the halves apart the bolt carrier is open to reach. Wipe the bolt and carrier clean of debris with solvent on a patch or a small rag, then put a light coat of oil on the bolt. Light means a film, not a puddle — excess oil only collects fouling.
steps.quote: Wipe the bolt clean of any debris with solvent and a patch or small rag. Lightly oil bolt.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.22

steps.title: Magazine follower and body cleaned, feed lips checked
steps.action: Brush the follower clean and wipe it and the magazine body with a solvent that is safe on plastic. Look over the feed lips for cracks or bends, and press the follower down to make sure it moves up and down freely. A damaged lip or a sticking follower is a feeding problem waiting to happen.
steps.quote: Routine maintenance consists of brushing the follower clean and using a plastic safe solvent to clean it and the magazine body.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, MAGAZINES, p.19

steps.title: Exposed metal filmed with oil, walnut wiped
steps.action: Coat every exposed metal surface with a light film of oil. After damp weather wipe the bore and metal dry and oil again; after soaking rain, snow or salt spray Henry calls for a more thorough clean. The walnut stock and forearm are sealed with a polyurethane finish and need little more than a wipe.
steps.quote: Make sure all exposed metal surfaces are coated with a film of oil.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.22

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The rifle is in two halves with the bolt carrier exposed on the rear half. That is Henry's field strip. If the bolt itself needs cleaning, Deep Clean follows Henry's bolt removal; otherwise move on to cleaning.
steps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, p.20

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin pulled out
deepSteps.action: Find the firing pin retaining pin toward the rear on the left-hand side of the bolt carrier and pull it out. Henry says a fingernail is enough — no punch, no pliers. Put it somewhere it cannot roll away; it is small.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin retaining pin located towards the rear lefthand side of the bolt carrier. This can be done with a fingernail.
deepSteps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — BOLT REMOVAL FOR CLEANING, p.20

deepSteps.title: Firing pin drawn out of the rear of the carrier
deepSteps.action: With its retaining pin out, the firing pin slides out of the back of the bolt carrier. Pull it straight out the rear and lay it with the retaining pin.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the firing pin free from the rear of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — BOLT REMOVAL FOR CLEANING, p.20

deepSteps.title: Cam pin lifted out of the top
deepSteps.action: Lift the cam pin out of its hole in the top of the bolt carrier. Note which way its ejector flange faces — it goes back only one way, with the flange to the left.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the cam pin from the top of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — BOLT REMOVAL FOR CLEANING, p.20

deepSteps.title: Bolt pulled out of the front of the carrier
deepSteps.action: The bolt now slides out of the front of the carrier. Wipe the bolt, the carrier bore and the firing pin clean with solvent on a patch, then oil the bolt lightly.
deepSteps.quote: The bolt can now be pulled free from the front of the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — BOLT REMOVAL FOR CLEANING, p.20

deepSteps.title: Magazine floor plate off for the spring and follower
deepSteps.action: To clean inside the magazine, push the button on its base and slide the floor plate forward, the way the bullet noses face. The spring is under tension — keep your thumb over it and your safety glasses on. Clean the spring and follower, then reverse the steps to close it up.
deepSteps.quote: The floor plate can also be removed by pushing the button on the base and sliding forward. That will allow access for cleaning of the spring and follower.
deepSteps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY RIFLE, MAGAZINES, p.19
deepSteps.warn: Safety glasses should be warn as many components are under spring tension.

deepSteps.title: No further disassembly
deepSteps.action: Henry's book stops at the bolt. The trigger, hammer, safety, lever linkage and extractor are on the parts list but the book gives no procedure for them, and Henry wants any further work done by a qualified gunsmith. Clean what is now open and go no further.
deepSteps.quote: We do not recommend any further disassembly of this firearm.
deepSteps.cite: Henry Lever Action Supreme | Instruction Manual For H023 Series Rifles — H23-300 01.24 — the form code and date code printed on the back cover — BOLT REMOVAL FOR CLEANING, p.20
deepSteps.warn: NOTICE! DO NOT ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS MANUAL.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Clean from the chamber end toward the muzzle, with a pull-through kit where possible
Never run a brush through the barrel first
Never dip a brush in solvent
Keep a rod off the muzzle crown

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Wipe the bolt and carrier clean with solvent on a patch or rag
Do not leave fired cases in the chamber

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Clean the follower and body with a plastic-safe solvent
Check the feed lips for damage
Check the follower moves up and down freely

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & WOOD
tasks: Coat all exposed metal with a light film of oil
Wipe the walnut stock and forearm
Do not store it in leather or heavy cloth, or with a plug in the barrel

reassembly: If the bolt was removed: push the bolt back into the carrier with its lugs facing forward and line the hole in the bolt up with the carrier's hole at the 12 o'clock position.
Insert the cam pin with its slot in line with the bolt axis — it goes in only one way, ejector flange facing left.

Slide the firing pin into the rear of the carrier and through the cam pin until it is flush with the rear of the carrier, then push the firing pin retaining pin back into its hole on the rear left-hand side.

With the bolt extended, rest the top half of the receiver on a padded surface and support it while you feed the bolt carrier on the rear half toward the chamber until the receiver pin holes line up. It may take a try or two to find the angle at which the carrier enters its raceway.
Insert the two receiver retaining pins and tap them home until they are flush with the receiver.
If the magazine floor plate was removed, refit the spring and follower and slide the floor plate back on in reverse order.
fncheck: With the rifle empty, no magazine in and no ammunition in the room, work the lever through a full stroke: it should open and close smoothly with the bolt running home. Pull the safety back to S on the cocked rifle and confirm it clicks in, then push it forward to the red dot. Henry says this model may be dry-fired, so with the muzzle in a safe direction press the trigger to confirm the hammer falls. Never check function with live ammunition.
